passage:
There was an empty field beside the community center. Some people wanted to build a parking lot. Others wanted a garden.
The town held a meeting. Drivers said parking was difficult. Parents said children needed a safe place to play. Older people wanted benches and shade.
Finally, the town chose a mixed plan. Part of the field became parking spaces, and part became a small garden with a walking path.
No group got everything it wanted, but most people got something they needed.
The field taught the town a common lesson: public space belongs to many people. Good decisions require listening not only to the loudest voice, but to different needs.
